rationales: A hard disk is secondary storage, not volatile primary memory.
A USB drive is non-volatile secondary storage.
RAM is volatile primary memory.
A CD is non-volatile secondary storage.
HTML has more than four heading levels.
HTML has more than five heading levels.
HTML provides six heading levels, from h1 to h6.
HTML has more than one heading level.
Cipher is a general term, not the name of the method used by Caesar.
The Vigenère cipher is a different encryption method.
Julius Caesar used the Caesar cipher to send secret messages to his soldiers and generals.
A hacker is a person, not an encryption method.
FTP is a file-transfer protocol, not an internet service provider.
SMTP is used to send email, not to provide internet access.
HTTP is a protocol for transferring web pages.
An ISP provides internet service to home users.
A packet is not identified by a virtual address in this context.
A common address is not the standard address used to route packets.
A real address is not the standard term for a packet's network address.
An IP address is used to identify and route packets across networks.
The .htm extension can be used for an HTML page.
The .html extension can be used for an HTML page.
Both .htm and .html are valid extensions for an HTML page.
.xhtml is a separate markup-language extension and is not the expected general HTML extension here.
A flash drive retains data without power.
A memory card retains data without power.
RAM is volatile memory, so it is not non-volatile.
A hard drive retains data without power.
Hacking can be a cyber crime when done without authorization.
Phishing is a cyber crime involving deceptive attempts to obtain information.
Identity theft is a cyber crime involving misuse of another person's identity.
Decryption is not inherently a cyber crime; it can be a legitimate process.
Logical principles are not the stated foundation of security systems here.
Simplicity may be useful in security design but is not the intended foundation.
Complexity alone does not form the foundation of a security system.
Ethical principles provide the foundation for responsible security systems.
Algorithm efficiency is commonly assessed using two metrics: time and space.
Four metrics are not the standard basis cited for measuring algorithm efficiency.
Five metrics are not the standard basis cited for measuring algorithm efficiency.
Six metrics are not the standard basis cited for measuring algorithm efficiency.
Routers connect networks, not software programs.
Routers connect multiple networks together.
People may use networks, but routers do not connect people as their technical function.
Places are not the technical units that routers connect.
Input is used to receive data, not to display values.
Output is used to display or present values.
Start marks the beginning of an algorithm or flowchart.
Goto indicates a transfer of control, not the display of values.
By the distributive law, (A+B)(A+C) = A + (B.C).
A.B + A.C simplifies to A(B+C), which is not generally equivalent to the given expression.
A.(B.C) is A.B.C and is not equivalent to the given expression.
A+(B+C) simplifies to A+B+C and is not equivalent to the given expression.
Electronic message describes a message, not the expansion of E-mail.
Electronic medium is not the expansion of E-mail.
E-mail stands for electronic mail.
Electrical mail is not the correct expansion of E-mail.
Piracy is the unauthorized copying or distribution of software.
Privacy concerns control over personal information, not unauthorized software copying.
Right means an entitlement and is not the term for unauthorized software copying.
Browsing means viewing or navigating online content, not making unauthorized software copies.
